content.text: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Clear Capital exists anywhere in the agreement. The only restrictive covenant is a mutual non-solicit (p0047), and the sole "Company shall not" language (p0020) is an IP use-scope limit on the Contractor's own pre-existing materials, not a limit on our business. Section 4(b) runs the other way — it preserves the Contractor's freedom to serve other clients.

input.quote: Company acknowledges that Contractor provides consulting and development services to other clients, and agrees that nothing in this Agreement shall be deemed or construed to prevent Contractor from delivering on such business.
input.rationale: This is a presence rule and the agreement contains no non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restriction binding Clear Capital, so it meets the preferred position (no restriction on Customer). Searches for "compet", "exclusiv", "solicit", "shall not", "may not"/"agrees not to" and field-of-use phrasings surfaced nothing restricting the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build. The only restrictive covenant is the mutual, one-year employee non-solicit in § 13 (p0047), which is a separate term and applies equally to both parties. The sole "Company shall not" language (p0020) is a scope-of-use limit on the Contractor's own pre-existing proprietary materials — an IP licence-scope matter, not a restraint on our business, and § 4(c) (p0021) grants us a perpetual licence to use that material in our business operations. Section 4(b) (p0019) runs in the opposite direction, preserving the Contractor's freedom to serve other clients, which is a restriction-free position for the vendor and not something we would flag. No redline required.
